etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English thirsti, from Old English þurstiġ, from Proto-Germanic *þurstugaz. Equivalent to thirst +‎ -y. Cognate with Dutch dorstig, German durstig.

definitions.definition: Needing to drink water or any liquid that can supply water.
(euphemistic) Craving alcohol; especially, experiencing some alcohol withdrawal.
(informal, uncommon) Causing thirst; giving one a need to drink.

quote.text: I had for dinner, or rather supper, a chicken done up some way with red pepper, which was very good but thirsty.

definitions.definition: (usually in the plural) One who is thirsty (for a drink, sex, alcohol, etc.).
